title: Which derived radar products did KTLX publish around a tornado report?
summary: Pull thirty minutes of NEXRAD Level III mesocyclone, storm-track, and echo-top files, lock them, and see that they are stored without a reader.

title: How high was Hurricane Helene's storm surge at Cedar Key?
summary: Subtract CO-OPS tide predictions from observed water levels to isolate the surge, find its peak, and time it against the HURDAT2 landfall.

title: Do hourly airport observations reproduce the daily summary?
summary: Pull three days of Local Climatological Data for one airport, separate report types, and compare hourly extremes with NCEI's daily summary.

title: How many tornadoes did 2024 bring, by rating?
summary: Pull the Storm Prediction Center's 2024 tornado file, keep one row per tornado, and count them by EF rating with the longest paths.

title: Was 2024 warmer or wetter than normal?
summary: Compare twelve months at Oklahoma City's airport with 1991–2020 station normals, including temperature-unit checks and monthly anomaly plots.

title: What did radar and satellites show around a reported tornado?
summary: Connect one Storm Events report to nearby NEXRAD and GOES observations, with explicit time matching and a plotted event context.

title: How can I preserve weather and streamflow inputs together?
summary: Fetch NOAA and USGS observations with one manifest, inspect the tables, and verify and restore the exact inputs.

title: How warm was the sea in a small area?
summary: Download four sea-surface-temperature grid cells, inspect their units, and plot the selected area.

title: How did temperature and rainfall vary through the year?
summary: Read monthly station observations, compare temperature and precipitation in two plots, and verify the source manifest.

title: What severe weather was reported in Oklahoma?
summary: Filter an annual Storm Events archive locally, plot report counts and damage ratings, and account for reporting limitations.

title: What does one weather radar volume show?
summary: Open a NEXRAD Level II volume, inspect its sweeps and reflectivity units, and plot a selected sweep.

title: What did a satellite see in infrared?
summary: Decode a GOES CONUS scene, inspect quality flags and scan coordinates, and plot brightness temperatures.

title: How warm and wet was a year at one airport?
summary: Fetch complete-year station summaries and read annual temperature and precipitation with a reproducible manifest.

title: What is normal weather for a month at one station?
summary: Read 1991–2020 monthly temperature and precipitation normals and select a month for comparison.

title: How high was the water at The Battery?
summary: Inspect three six-minute coastal observations, their reference datum, quality flags, and source provenance.

title: How can I inspect Atlantic hurricane tracks?
summary: Read the whole Atlantic best-track file, identify hurricane-intensity landfall records, and inspect peak winds and historical coverage limits.

title: Did lightning near the storm pick up before the Oklahoma City tornado report?
summary: Count GOES-16 GLM flashes minute by minute in a fixed box around the report over the hour ending at it, against a same-size control box and the whole field of view.

title: Where was the strongest mid-level rotation in each two-minute grid, and did it move toward the reported tornado?
summary: Locate the strongest MRMS mid-level azimuthal shear in each two-minute grid inside two boxes around the report and measure how far each peak sat from the reported path start.

title: What did the HRRR analysis say about the storm environment over central Oklahoma at 20 UTC, and how far was the tornado report from the most favorable values?
summary: Read surface CAPE and 0-3 km helicity from one HRRR analysis at the grid point nearest the report, find the largest values within 100 km, and map both fields.

title: What did the global model say the environment was before a reported tornado?
summary: Pull the GFS 00 UTC 1-degree analysis for 2024-05-06 and read surface CAPE and 0-3 km helicity at the grid point nearest Oklahoma City.

title: Which severe reports came with rotation and lightning?
summary: Convert one Oklahoma tornado report to UTC, join it to the nearest NEXRAD volume, MRMS rotation track, and GLM flashes, then build a small labeled table of rotation and lightning features for tornado, hail, and wind reports from the same evening.
